newsitem.title: USA: Baseball's Schott agrees to sell auto dealership.
newsitem.headline: Baseball's Schott agrees to sell auto dealership.

text.p: Controversial baseball owner Marge Schott, under fire from General Motors Corp for allegedly falsifying auto sales records, will sell her Chevrolet-Geo dealership, the dealership said Wednesday.

"She sent a letter to Chevrolet giving notice that she had decided not to continue as a Chevrolet dealer after 16 years of service," dealership general manager Mike Horvath said Wednesday, reading from a prepared statement.
Major League Baseball's only female team owner remained suspended from day-to-day operations of the Cincinnati Reds through 1998 after racially insensitive remarks she made in interviews last year.
Horvath said she agreed to sell her Chevrolet franchise to a family that owns other dealerships in the Cincinnati area.
She will retain a Buick dealership she has owned since her husband Charlie died 28 years ago. General Motors spokesman Kyle Johnson said GM has no objection to that.
But GM must approve any new owner for the Chevy franchise and had not received any paperwork yet from Schott, he said.

GM, seeking to terminate her as a Chevy dealer, alleged in a document filed with the Ohio dealer licensing board that Schott, 68, falsified 1995 sales records to meet sales goals, listing 57 transactions that never occurred.
GM said Schott used names of acquaintances and dealership personnel as fictitious car buyers then hid the unsold cars on her estate, selling at least one of them later as a used car.
The National League is studying the case to see if league action is warranted.
